Scoring probability and expected points along one variable

Source: R/curves.R
shot_curve.Rd

Nadaraya-Watson Gaussian kernel smoothing, with two additions that make the curve readable: a bootstrap confidence band, so a wiggle can be told apart from noise, and the density of attempts, so the curve can be drawn thick where shots actually happen and thin where it rests on a handful of attempts.

Usage

shot_curve(
  shots,
  x,
  by = NULL,
  outcome = c("prob", "points"),
  bw = NULL,
  n_boot = 200,
  level = 0.9,
  grid = NULL,
  min_density = 0.02,
  split_value = FALSE
)

Arguments

shots

A data frame with made and the variable x; for expected points also value (or pts).

x

Name of the variable (e.g. "dist", "playlength", "periodTime"). "dist" is computed from x, y if absent.

by

Optional grouping column (e.g. "player").

outcome

"prob" (scoring probability) or "points" (expected points per shot).

bw

Kernel bandwidth in units of x. Default: Silverman's rule on the pooled data.

n_boot

Bootstrap resamples for the band (0 to skip).

level

Width of the band.

grid

Points at which to evaluate; default 100 points over the central 99% of x.

min_density

Grid points where a group's attempt density falls below this fraction of its peak are dropped, so curves are not extrapolated into places a player never shoots from.

split_value

Smooth 2-point and 3-point attempts separately. A kernel smoother run across the 3-point line blurs the jump in value into a fake ramp; splitting keeps the discontinuity (use with distance).

Value

A tibble with x, estimate, lower, upper, density and the grouping column.

Examples

sc <- shot_curve(subset(shots_2024, league == "NBA"), "dist", outcome = "points", n_boot = 0)
head(sc)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>       x estimate lower upper density attempts
#>   <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>    <int>
#> 1 0         1.43    NA    NA   0.533   219527
#> 2 0.101     1.41    NA    NA   0.612   219527
#> 3 0.201     1.40    NA    NA   0.684   219527
#> 4 0.302     1.38    NA    NA   0.747   219527
#> 5 0.402     1.36    NA    NA   0.796   219527
#> 6 0.503     1.33    NA    NA   0.830   219527
